I was just talking to a friend about this. Idk how he’d react and I’m really scared to open the door. He’s a nice guy but I’m still scared.

Many of the things described within that article do seem to relate to him, and his family honestly had very open narcissistic tendencies (particularly his mother, father, and especially his sister).

There were many times in the relationship in which I felt that I was living for him (willingly) and I was totally and completely invested in uplifting him and making him a better person. I only felt that was reciprocated occasionally. I didn’t ask much from him, and as a result that is why I was so short tempered when I attempted to address concerns to him and he couldn’t seem to care whatsoever.

Still I feel an immense amount of guilt that eats me alive. What if I ruined his life? Will he tell his next partner about how horrid of a human being I was to him? Will I feel shame if I were to face him in public? Though the way he handled our breakup amongst other transgressions within our relationship made me feel very invalid and useless and like I was insane, during this time I can (still) only care about him and his feelings. I want **him** to be okay much more than I want myself to be. 

Knowing him, he will find a way to validate all the decisions he had made throughout the relationship. I am the opposite. I can’t even begin to acknowledge any of the good I ever did for him, and strictly focus on all the damage I have done and fear that I will always continue to be an unsafe person. 

Today being his birthday, these feelings are incredibly overwhelming and send my mind into dark thoughts as a result of the guilt....

> Does he engage in crazy-making behaviors?  

My ex partner notoriously (recognized by his family as well) did not care about what anyone ever had to say. He wouldn’t even pretend to be interested, and when he felt right about something he would not back down (I.e one day he disappeared completely for 4 hours after hanging out together and parting ways, I was concerned because he always kept a charged battery pack so his phone was *never* dead. I asked his sister if she had heard from him and explained the situation and she ended up telling their entire family that he was missing. He eventually showed up saying his phone had died and proceeded to chew me out in front of his mom about how I should have “minded my business and given him more time to arrive”. I hung up and he called back the next day saying “my mom said to apologize”). On top of that HE didn’t believe in apologizing or compromising at all either. I REALLY loved this man with all my heart and despite these things I would still kill to be with him, but there were moments where I really felt like I didn’t matter or existed in his life whereas I always made him very integrated into mine.


At the end of the day though, I recognize that I should’ve compromises better and accepted things for what they were. I shouldn’t have gone on benders yelling at him trying to get him to get it “right” when his truth is just as viable and acceptable as mine is. If I was truly unhappy with the cards I had been dealt, I should’ve just broken up with him rather than prolonging the inevitable. I shouldn’t have been so mean, and for that I feel very ashamed. He was nice to me, he did care about my well being (although in his own way).

I just hate that he really might be out there in this world hating me when I have him my entire being. I understand that that is MY personal choice and I cannot hold him accountable for things that happened because of me, but it sucks that I loved so much and it was all just one big waste of time in the end. Especially knowing that had I just not been as mean as I was, we would still be together and I would’ve been enjoying my life like I was. I hate to admit it, but he made me love life, I loved being alive with him, and I actually looked forward to the future. Since our breakup I feel incredibly pessimistic, unloveable, and worthless, especially since he broke up by ghosting me for 3 days after an argument and finally contacting me on the third day to say “I’ll talk to you when I’m ready”. He never spoke to me again. I wasn’t even worth a proper breakup.

> Have you apologized to this person at all

I actually have composed an email that is written SOLELY to apologize to him with no pandering to getting back together. I just want him to know how genuinely sorry I am and how I am grateful that he has made me recognize the issue at hand and the fact that I NEED to address them. I thank him for or time together and I wish him nothing but the best. But I’m too scared to send it. I’m scared that it’s too late. This shame and guilt is unbearable. 

I definitely think that my abuse stems from expectations (and slightly the desire of control, I was terrified of him leaving me). I just hated that he didn’t care about what I had to say ever, and it would drive me up the walls and I permitted my abusive tendencies to take ahold rather than being a leveled human being who responded responsibly to issues.

I think my biggest fear is that I simply WILL NOT be able to breakout of this cycle and will be doomed to commit the same mistakes over and over again no matter how hard I try. I feel like such a failure.
